title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan to Lead ‘Sapt Dhara of Shakti’ Pledge at Pusa on August 18
subtitle:
Shivraj Singh Chouhan to Chart Roadmap for Agriculture & Rural Development Towards Viksit Bharat 2047
Farmers, Lakhpati Didis, Exporters & Food Processors to Join ‘Sapt Dhara of Shakti’ Pledge
6 Crore Lakhpati Didis, Stronger Agriculture: ‘Sapt Dhara of Shakti’ to Drive Rural Development Agenda
body_text:
Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan will administer a pledge to officials of both ministries at the Pusa campus in New Delhi on August 18, following the “Sapt Dhara of Shakti” outlined by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in his Independence Day address on August 15. The program will focus on the roadmap of various departments, the expansion of the Lakhpati Didi program and important decisions concerning the interests of farmers and rural communities. The meeting aims to translate the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047 into a clear and actionable roadmap for agriculture and rural development. Progressive farmers, Lakhpati Didis, agricultural exporters and food processors will also participate in the program.
Shri Chouhan said that the “Sapt Dhara of Shakti” outlined by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi provides an important direction for agriculture and rural India. He said the government would work to turn this vision into action through people-centric programs, transparent monitoring and effective implementation. “Our aim is to ensure that farmers and rural women benefit directly and that our efforts contribute to the realisation of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. In this direction, we will review the departmental roadmaps and work to accelerate their implementation,” Shri Chouhan said.
In his Independence Day address from the Red Fort, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi outlined the “Sapt Dhara of Shakti”, which includes strengthening agriculture and food production, promoting food processing and expanding access to global markets as important priorities. The Prime Minister also reiterated the government’s commitment to providing fertilisers to farmers at subsidised prices amid global crises and uncertainties. He highlighted the need to create new global markets and opportunities for farmers, particularly in agriculture and marine products, including seafood. The focus on self-reliance also forms an important part of the agenda. The Prime Minister highlighted the long-term measures undertaken over the past decade to ensure that India remains secure and self-reliant in essential requirements such as fertilisers and fuel, particularly in the face of global uncertainties.
Focus on Expanding Lakhpati Didi
The Lakhpati Didi program of the Ministry of Rural Development will be an important focus of the August 18 meeting. Three crore rural women have already become Lakhpati Didis, and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has set a new target of taking this number to six crore. Shri Chouhan will discuss the implementation roadmap for expanding the programme and achieving this target. Women associated with Self-Help Groups are being supported through skill development and financial assistance to strengthen their livelihoods and increase their incomes. Women’s empowerment and economic independence are central to the government’s approach to rural development. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has also called upon citizens to recognise and respect the capabilities of women and support their greater participation in economic development.
To strengthen market access for women-led enterprises, initiatives such as She-Marts have also been included in the Union Budget. These initiatives are aimed at helping women find better markets for their products and build stronger rural enterprises. Through She-Marts and branding initiatives, products linked to yoga, Ayurveda, handicrafts and other rural enterprises will be promoted for wider domestic and global markets. Creating stronger market opportunities for products made by rural women will remain an important priority as the government works towards the next phase of women-led rural development.

enrichment.summary: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will administer a 'Sapt Dhara of Shakti' pledge to Agriculture and Rural Development ministry officials at Pusa, New Delhi on August 18, 2026, following PM Modi's Independence Day announcement of seven priority areas for agriculture and rural development. The event will focus on expanding the Lakhpati Didi programme from 3 crore to a new target of 6 crore rural women, alongside roadmaps for food processing, farmer welfare, and market access initiatives like She-Marts.
enrichment.context:
The 'Sapt Dhara of Shakti' (Seven Streams of Strength) was outlined by PM Modi in his 2026 Independence Day address as a framework covering agriculture and food production, food processing, subsidised fertilisers, global market access for agricultural and marine products, and self-reliance in essential inputs. This event operationalises that vision through an administrative pledge and ministerial roadmap review rather than announcing new schemes itself.

The Lakhpati Didi scheme, launched under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), aims to enable rural women in Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to earn a sustainable annual income of at least Rs 1 lakh through skill development, financial support, and livelihood diversification. The scheme has been a flagship women's economic empowerment initiative, with the target progressively raised from 2 crore to 3 crore and now to 6 crore, reflecting its scaling up as a rural development priority. She-Marts, referenced in the Union Budget, represent a newer market-linkage initiative to help women-led enterprises access better markets for products such as handicrafts, Ayurveda, and yoga-related goods, complementing existing SHG market platforms.

prelims.why_important: Numerical targets and their revisions are a favourite UPSC prelims trap for testing attentiveness to current updates.

prelims.point: 'Sapt Dhara of Shakti' (Seven Streams of Strength) was announced by PM Modi in his 2026 Independence Day address, covering agriculture/food production, food processing, subsidised fertilisers, global market access for agri/marine products, and self-reliance in essential inputs.
